entries.h: A client at 34 weeks with preeclampsia reports "the worst headache of my life." BP is 162/104. She is awake, talking and has not had a seizure. How does the nurse classify her condition?
entries.t: Answer Preeclampsia with a severe feature: a warning symptom and a severe-range systolic pressure ↓ Reasoning Eclampsia means a new seizure. Clinical detail A severe headache is a warning symptom, and a systolic of 160 or more is severe range, so this is preeclampsia with severe features: report it now and keep seizure precautions in place. It is not eclampsia until she seizes, and the diastolic does not need to reach 110 when the systolic is already 160 or more. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Simple Nursing · Seizures and epilepsy (13:04) Why the other answers do not fit Eclampsia, because a severe headache with severe-range BP is eclampsia A severe headache is a warning symptom, and a systolic of 160 or more is severe range, so this is preeclampsia with severe features: report it now and keep seizure precautions in place. Eclampsia, because her systolic pressure is above 160 It is not eclampsia until she seizes, and the diastolic does not need to reach 110 when the systolic is already 160 or more. Gestational hypertension only, because her diastolic pressure is under 110 It is not eclampsia until she seizes, and the diastolic does not need to reach 110 when the systolic is already 160 or more. Original Study Hub illustration · Preeclampsia versus eclampsia, the same spectrum with different presentations. Preeclampsia is new hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or qualifying organ dysfunction, can develop postpartum, and proteinuria is not required when other diagnostic features are present. Eclampsia is new seizures associated with preeclampsia when another cause does not explain them, and can occur without previously recognised preeclampsia. entries.h: A client with bipolar I disorder has had progressively more frequent and severe manic episodes over 15 years with shorter well intervals. Which concept explains this pattern?
entries.t: Answer Kindling ↓ Reasoning Kindling describes how each mood episode lowers the threshold for the next through progressive neuronal sensitization, so untreated episodes beget more frequent and more autonomous episodes. Clinical detail Tolerance is a reduced drug effect, extinction is the fading of a conditioned response, and downregulation is a decrease in receptor number. This is the strongest argument the nurse can give for maintenance mood stabilizer therapy even when the client feels well. entries.h: Match each finding to the condition it best represents.
entries.t: What the finding means The pill-rolling tremor, masklike face, and shuffling gait are classic Parkinson's disease findings. entries.h: A school bus and a truck have collided. Emergency medical services has declared a mass casualty incident and is using START triage. A nurse is triaging adults pulled from the bus. One man did not walk to the collection area. His respirations are 36, he has no palpable radial pulse, and he does not follow simple commands.
entries.t: What the finding means Under START, any one of three findings makes a victim immediate: respirations of 30 or more, an absent radial pulse or capillary refill longer than 2 seconds, or an inability to follow simple commands. Clinical detail He has all three, so the tempting answer of delayed is wrong on every criterion. The only care given during START is opening the airway and controlling major bleeding, because starting an intravenous line pulls the triager away from victims no one has assessed yet. entries.h: A 10-year-old received a new long-arm cast for a forearm fracture 6 hours ago. He reports severe pain unrelieved by his prescribed opioid, and the pain worsens when the nurse passively extends his fingers. His fingers are pale and cool with delayed capillary refill.
entries.t: What the finding means Pain unrelieved by analgesics and worsened by passive movement, along with pallor and cool skin, are early findings of compartment syndrome, a limb-threatening complication in which pressure inside a closed space such as a cast compresses nerves, vessels, and muscle and can cause permanent damage if not relieved quickly. Clinical detail Ordinary post-fracture pain responds to prescribed analgesics and does not specifically worsen with passive stretch. An allergic reaction to padding would cause itching or a rash rather than pain and pallor, and infection under a cast this soon after placement typically presents with warmth and fever rather than pallor and delayed capillary refill. entries.h: A 30-year-old woman is brought in by police after threatening neighbors with a knife. She refuses evaluation and tries to walk out. She is shouting, pacing, and has thrown a chair. Verbal de-escalation and an offer of oral medication have both failed. The provider writes an order for physical restraint for violent behavior.
entries.t: What the finding means Emergency psychiatric holds are created by state statute, and states differ on the permitted length, the criteria, and who is allowed to initiate one, so her state's law and the facility policy give the specific answer. Clinical detail The Medicare conditions of participation cap renewal of a violent-behavior restraint order at 4 hours for adults 18 and older, 2 hours for ages 9 through 17, and 1 hour under age 9, for up to 24 hours total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour of initiation. A relative cannot consent to detain another adult, and waiting for a court order would leave an actively dangerous situation unmanaged. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client hospitalized with acute diverticulitis. To reduce the risk of COMPLICATIONS, which nursing interventions should the nurse implement? Select all that apply.

entries.h: A client is receiving continuous bladder irrigation on the unit after transurethral resection of the prostate. Which finding requires immediate action?
entries.t: Correct answer No urine output for one hour with lower abdominal distension Why Absent drainage with lower abdominal distension suggests an obstructed catheter. Pause inflow to avoid further distension, check the drainage tubing, and obtain urgent help to restore outflow according to protocol. Never wait an hour to respond to a catheter that stops draining. Why the other answers do not fit Pink-tinged urine A pink tinge can occur after resection. The immediate threat here is accumulating fluid behind an obstruction. Bladder spasms relieved by the prescribed medication A brief, relieved bladder spasm can reflect catheter irritation. Persistent pain or spasms with reduced outflow require reassessment. Small clots in the drainage on the first day Small clots may pass early when drainage remains free. Increasing clots, heavy bleeding, or interruption of flow changes the priority. entries.h: A 19-year-old client with asthma is admitted to the medical unit with wheezing and chest tightness. He is prescribed albuterol and fluticasone, both by metered-dose inhaler, at the same scheduled time. Which action by the nurse is correct?
entries.t: Answer Give the albuterol first, wait 5 minutes, then give the fluticasone. ↓ Reasoning Albuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist that opens the airways in minutes, so the steroid can then reach deeper lung tissue. entries.h: A client is very difficult to arouse, has steadily decreasing vital signs, and is getting the deepest physical rest of the night. The nurse should document that the client is in which stage of sleep?
entries.t: Answer Stage 3 NREM ↓ Reasoning Stage 3 NREM is slow wave or delta sleep, when vital signs steadily fall, sympathetic activity drops, and physical restoration occurs. Clinical detail REM is the tempting choice because arousal is also difficult in REM, but REM brings fluctuating vital signs, vivid dreaming, and cognitive rather than physical restoration. entries.h: Match each distinguishing feature to the condition it best represents.
entries.t: What the finding means Gout causes acute, intensely painful monoarticular attacks classically in the great toe. Clinical detail Fibromyalgia produces widespread pain and fatigue without joint swelling or deformity on exam. Rheumatoid arthritis causes symmetric joint involvement with deformities like ulnar deviation and prolonged morning stiffness. Lupus is confirmed by a positive ANA along with depleted C3 and C4 complement from immune complex activity. Osteoarthritis is not used because none of these vignettes describe the asymmetric, activity-related joint pain typical of degenerative joint disease. entries.h: A 79-year-old woman admitted with pneumonia has gotten up alone twice tonight to reach the bathroom. She uses a walker at home, takes a daily diuretic, and fell in her kitchen three months ago. She is oriented and says she did not want to bother anyone.
entries.t: What the finding means Scheduled toileting with the walker in reach is the least restrictive measure and it addresses the actual trigger, which is a diuretic and a full bladder. Clinical detail A low bed with locked wheels shortens the distance if she does slip. Raising all four side rails to keep a client from getting out of bed meets the federal definition of a restraint, which is why it is the trap. Telling her not to get up does not work when the urge is real and she is trying not to be a burden. entries.h: Highlight the findings that show the antidepressant is working.
entries.t: What the finding means Response to an antidepressant is measured by the return of sleep, appetite, weight, and social activity together with a falling depression score, and a PHQ-9 moving from 21 to 8 crosses from severe into the mild range. Clinical detail Hard mornings are a residual symptom rather than proof of failure, and full response often takes longer than six weeks. Normal vital signs and the absence of nausea show the drug is tolerated, which is the tempting one to pick and a different question from whether it worked. entries.h: Which finding best distinguishes normal grief from major depressive disorder?
entries.t: Answer The client's self-esteem remains intact and the focus is on the loss ↓ Reasoning Sleep, appetite, and crying occur in both. Clinical detail The discriminators are self-esteem and focus: in grief the client feels bad about the loss and can still be comforted and laugh in waves; in depression the client feels worthless, the focus turns inward, and the mood is unrelenting. Thoughts of death in grief tend toward joining the deceased; in depression toward dying because life has no value. entries.h: A 59-year-old man on oral theophylline calls the clinic reporting nausea, vomiting, a pounding heartbeat, and feeling jittery. He mentions he has been drinking several energy drinks daily to stay awake at work. His theophylline level drawn that morning is 26 mcg/mL. Which action does the nurse take FIRST?
entries.t: Answer Instruct him to hold the next dose and come in immediately, and notify the provider. ↓ Reasoning Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range of roughly 10 to 20 mcg/mL, so 26 is toxic. Clinical detail Nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and restlessness are classic toxicity signs and seizures can follow, so the drug is held and the provider is notified now. Caffeine and energy drinks add to the stimulant effect and must be avoided, and taking the dose with food or adding a dose would only push the level higher. THEOPHYLLINE 10 TO 20; ABOVE THAT MEANS NAUSEA, TACHYCARDIA, SEIZURES. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Simple Nursing · Seizures and epilepsy (13:04) Why the other answers do not fit Tell him this level is therapeutic and the symptoms are unrelated. Advise him to take the next dose with food to settle his stomach. Caffeine and energy drinks add to the stimulant effect and must be avoided, and taking the dose with food or adding a dose would only push the level higher. Suggest he add an extra dose since his symptoms suggest poor control. Shared reasoning for choices without a separate note: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range of roughly 10 to 20 mcg/mL, so 26 is toxic. entries.h: A client admitted with acute diverticulitis is suspected of having a ruptured diverticulum and is now developing peritonitis. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Keep the client NPO Administer IV broad-spectrum antibiotics as prescribed Begin IV fluid replacement Prepare the client for possible surgery ↓ Reasoning THE BOWEL HAS RUPTURED, SO IT MUST REST (NPO), THE SPILLED BACTERIA MUST BE COVERED (IV BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBIOTICS), THE LOST FLUID MUST BE REPLACED (IV FLUIDS), AND THE HOLE MUST BE CLOSED (SURGERY). Clinical detail Antibiotics cannot close a hole - surgery is the only way to fix something that has popped, burst, or ruptured inside the body. entries.h: Which clients are at increased risk for developing a pulmonary embolism? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers A client in a long leg cast for a fractured tibia A client taking combined hormonal birth control A client on tamoxifen for breast cancer A client with a BMI of 34 ↓ Reasoning The tibia fracture causes immobility and venous stasis, and estrogen exposure raises clotting risk, which is why hormonal contraceptives and tamoxifen, a selective estrogen-receptor modulator, both count. entries.h: A nurse hears loud, wet, gurgling respirations in a client who is unresponsive and within hours of death. Which action should the nurse take first?

entries.h: Which observations are early cues of escalating agitation?

entries.h: A nurse is planning to collect a specimen from a male infant using a urine collection bag. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
entries.t: Answer Wash and dry the infant's genitalia and perineum thoroughly. ↓ Reasoning The bag is adhesive , so the skin has to be clean and completely dry for it to seal — a damp or greasy perineum means the specimen leaks into the diaper. Clinical detail Lubricant does exactly what the nurse is trying to avoid: no oil, lotion, powder or lubricant goes anywhere near the skin. In a boy the penis and the scrotum both go inside the bag , with the adhesive started at the bridge of skin between the anus and the scrotum. And the bag is checked every 20–30 minutes and removed as soon as the infant voids — waiting hours contaminates the sample and macerates the skin. Remember a bagged specimen is not sterile: it is acceptable for a urinalysis , but a culture needs a catheterized specimen. Wait several hours after positioning the device before checking it. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client hospitalized with acute diverticulitis. To reduce the risk of COMPLICATIONS, which nursing interventions should the nurse implement?

entries.h: A 68-year-old woman has taken scheduled oxycodone since a wrist fracture. No formed stool for four days. Abdomen firm and distended with hypoactive bowel sounds. Small smears of liquid brown stool are in her brief. She is passing little flatus, has no vomiting, and her appetite has dropped. Temperature 36.9 degrees C, heart rate 88, blood pressure 126/74.
entries.t: What the finding means Liquid stool leaking around a hard mass is overflow seepage, not diarrhea, and opioids slow gut motility enough to produce it within days. Clinical detail Distention with hypoactive sounds and almost no flatus makes impaction the leading problem over infection or retention, though she is still passing some gas, which argues against a complete obstruction. Checking the rectum where policy permits and giving the prescribed softener with a stimulant treat the real problem, and the next documented stool with a softening abdomen shows it worked. entries.h: Which contraindication should the nurse check for before giving the MMR vaccine?

entries.h: A client with endometriosis says a relative told her to "just get pregnant and it will fix itself." What is the nurse's best response?
entries.t: Answer "Pregnancy can quiet the symptoms while it lasts, but it is not a treatment — and endometriosis itself can make conceiving harder." ↓ Reasoning The disease is estrogen-dependent , so pregnancy and menopause do quiet it — but pregnancy is not a treatment, and it is thoughtless advice to give someone whose disease is a leading cause of infertility . Clinical detail Hysterectomy with removal of the ovaries is definitive but ends fertility and causes surgical menopause; it is a last resort, not the only option. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Why the other answers do not fit "That is good advice — pregnancy cures endometriosis." Hysterectomy with removal of the ovaries is definitive but ends fertility and causes surgical menopause; it is a last resort, not the only option. Original Study Hub illustration · Endometriosis: tissue outside the uterus. A female pelvic anatomy diagram labels normal endometrium inside the uterine cavity and endometriosis lesions on the outer uterine surface, an ovary, the pelvic lining and the fallopian tube, with an ovarian endometrioma labelled as a chocolate cyst and an adhesion. Symptoms listed: painful periods, chronic pelvic pain, deep pain with sex, bowel and bladder pain especially during periods, fatigue and possible fertility difficulty, and that some people have very few symptoms. Assessment: pain and menstrual history, pelvic examination and imaging such as ultrasound or MRI, normal imaging does not exclude endometriosis, and a clinical diagnosis can guide treatment while laparoscopy may be appropriate in selected cases. Treatment depends on symptoms and fertility goals: pain relief, hormonal suppression, surgery, with supportive symptom tracking and pelvic floor or pain care. Key distinctions: endometriosis occurs outside the uterus, adenomyosis occurs within the uterine muscle, pregnancy and hysterectomy are not guaranteed cures, and pain severity does not reliably match lesion extent. entries.h: Which instructions should the nurse give a client going home after laparoscopic treatment of endometriosis? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers No heavy lifting for about 2 weeks Nothing in the vagina for about 2 weeks — no tampons, douching or intercourse Report fever, heavy bleeding or worsening abdominal pain Warm compresses may ease discomfort ↓ Reasoning Two weeks is the number: no heavy lifting and nothing in the vagina while the sites heal. Clinical detail Warm compresses help. Fever, heavy bleeding or worsening pain are the call-the-provider findings. Shower rather than soak while the port sites heal, and conservative surgery relieves the disease — it does not cure it, and implants can return. A female pelvic anatomy diagram labels normal endometrium inside the uterine cavity and endometriosis lesions on the outer uterine surface, an ovary, the pelvic lining and the fallopian tube, with an ovarian endometrioma labelled as a chocolate cyst and an adhesion. Symptoms listed: painful periods, chronic pelvic pain, deep pain with sex, bowel and bladder pain especially during periods, fatigue and possible fertility difficulty, and that some people have very few symptoms. Assessment: pain and menstrual history, pelvic examination and imaging such as ultrasound or MRI, normal imaging does not exclude endometriosis, and a clinical diagnosis can guide treatment while laparoscopy may be appropriate in selected cases. Treatment depends on symptoms and fertility goals: pain relief, hormonal suppression, surgery, with supportive symptom tracking and pelvic floor or pain care. Key distinctions: endometriosis occurs outside the uterus, adenomyosis occurs within the uterine muscle, pregnancy and hysterectomy are not guaranteed cures, and pain severity does not reliably match lesion extent. entries.h: A client with a long history of alcohol use disorder presents with confusion, nystagmus, and ataxia. Which statements about this presentation are accurate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers The underlying cause is thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency Thiamine should be given before or with intravenous glucose Untreated Wernicke encephalopathy can progress to Korsakoff syndrome Korsakoff syndrome features severe anterograde amnesia with confabulation Korsakoff-related memory damage is often permanent ↓ Reasoning Wernicke encephalopathy is an acute thiamine deficiency emergency presenting with the triad of confusion, oculomotor changes such as nystagmus, and ataxia, and it is reversible if thiamine is given promptly. entries.h: A 28-year-old woman with panic disorder had chest tightness, a pounding heart, and a fear she was dying while in the waiting room. At 1005 her HR was 126 and RR 30. entries.h: Why does a ventricular septal defect produce a loud, harsh murmur without making the infant cyanotic?
entries.t: Answer Blood is forced from the higher-pressure left ventricle into the right, so it still reaches the lungs ↓ Reasoning A VSD is a left-to-right shunt . Clinical detail The left ventricle runs at much higher pressure, so blood is pushed across the hole into the right side and on to the lungs - noisy, but still oxygenated, so she is not blue . What she gets instead is too much pulmonary blood flow and heart failure : tiring with feeds, sweating, poor weight gain. Treated with furosemide and digoxin , and many close on their own. The cyanotic defects are the right-to-left ones - tetralogy of Fallot and tricuspid atresia. entries.h: A healthy 18-year-old who is up to date on childhood immunizations is moving into a college dormitory. Which vaccine should the nurse anticipate administering?
entries.t: Answer Meningococcal ↓ Reasoning Meningococcal — crowded residential living is the classic risk setting, and a first-year student living in a dormitory is the group the recommendation names. entries.h: A client on haloperidol develops temperature 40.1 C, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental status, and creatine kinase of 4,200. Which statements about this condition are correct? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers The mechanism is abrupt, massive dopamine D2 blockade Elevated creatine kinase reflects rhabdomyolysis from sustained muscle rigidity Acute kidney injury from myoglobinuria is a major risk The antipsychotic should be stopped immediately Dantrolene and bromocriptine may be used in treatment ↓ Reasoning Neuroleptic malignant syndrome results from profound D2 blockade causing hyperthermia and lead-pipe rigidity ; the rigidity destroys muscle, raising CK and releasing myoglobin that injures the kidneys, so treatment is stopping the drug, aggressive cooling and hydration, dantrolene for muscle relaxation, and bromocriptine as a dopamine agonist. entries.h: The nurse is caring for a client who has just returned to the unit after a colon resection. The client is showing signs of hypoxia. The nurse knows that this is probably caused by:
entries.t: Answer shunting. ↓ Reasoning Shunting appears to be the main cause of hypoxia after thoracic or abdominal surgery and most types of respiratory failure. entries.h: A client who abruptly stopped long-term prednisone 2 days ago is brought to the emergency department. Blood pressure is 88/54 mm Hg , heart rate is 118/min . Labs show an elevated potassium level, a low sodium level, and a low glucose level.
entries.t: What the finding means Abrupt corticosteroid withdrawal removes the body's exogenous cortisol source and can precipitate an Addisonian crisis, which presents with hypotension, tachycardia, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and hypoglycemia, exactly as described. Clinical detail The priority is rapid IV isotonic fluid resuscitation plus IV hydrocortisone to restore volume and replace cortisol; fluid restriction and a diuretic would worsen the existing hypovolemia and hypotension. Cushing syndrome would produce the opposite picture (hypertension, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia), so it does not fit this presentation. entries.h: A nurse is teaching a client about the potential complications of frequent laxative use. Which should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Electrolyte imbalances Dehydration Bowel dependence Impaired absorption of medications ↓ Reasoning Frequent laxative use → diarrhea → fluid and electrolyte losses (especially K⁺ and Na⁺) and dehydration. entries.h: A nurse is teaching a client about hernia care. Which interventions apply to PREOPERATIVE hernia care? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Wear a truss pad during waking hours Avoid lifting objects greater than 10 pounds Prevent constipation with fiber and fluids ↓ Reasoning A truss supports the weakened abdominal wall and is worn while UPRIGHT (lying down already relieves the pressure) — it’s preoperative only, since the repair makes it unnecessary. Clinical detail Avoiding heavy lifting and preventing constipation both apply BEFORE and AFTER surgery: before, straining and lifting can push the hernia out and cause a STRANGULATED hernia; after, the same forces threaten the repair with dehiscence. Teach the client that a hernia they cannot push back in, especially with severe pain, is a STRANGULATED hernia and an emergency. Risk factors: male, older age, chronic constipation, chronic cough (COPD), and heavy lifting. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client hospitalized with acute diverticulitis. To reduce the risk of COMPLICATIONS, which nursing interventions should the nurse implement?

entries.h: A nurse is assessing a client with a suspected bowel obstruction. Which findings are most consistent with a LARGE bowel obstruction rather than a small bowel obstruction? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Significant lower abdominal distension Diarrhea leaking around an impaction Only minor fluid and electrolyte imbalance ↓ Reasoning The whole distinction comes down to one idea: a SMALL bowel obstruction can decompress itself by VOMITING; a large bowel obstruction cannot, because the ileocecal valve blocks backflow. Clinical detail So LARGE bowel → marked lower abdominal distension, stool impaction with liquid diarrhea leaking around it, and only mild fluid/electrolyte disturbance. SMALL bowel → profuse feculent vomiting, and losing gastric acid produces METABOLIC ALKALOSIS with rapid dehydration and electrolyte loss. High-pitched tympanic bowel sounds above the blockage and obstipation occur in BOTH, so they don’t help you tell them apart — which is exactly why they’re in the option list. entries.h: A nurse is teaching a client who was newly diagnosed with diverticulosis after a routine colonoscopy. The client has no fever, no pain, and a normal white blood cell count. Which instruction should the nurse include?
entries.t: Answer Increase dietary fiber and fluids and avoid straining during bowel movements ↓ Reasoning OSIS MEANS THE POUCHES ARE THERE BUT ARE NOT INFLAMED - there is no infection to treat yet. entries.h: Which client statements indicate the teaching was NOT understood?

entries.h: A client has partial-thickness burns over the entire anterior trunk and the anterior surface of the right arm. Using the rule of nines, what is the total body surface area burned?
entries.t: Answer 22.5% ↓ Reasoning Anterior trunk = 18% and an anterior arm = 4.5% (a whole arm is 9%, so the front of one is half). 18 + 4.5 = 22.5% . entries.h: Which nursing approaches are appropriate for a client with delusions? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers State your own perception once, calmly, without arguing Focus on the feeling underlying the delusion Redirect to reality-based topics and activities Avoid whispering or laughing where the client can see but not hear you ↓ Reasoning Do not argue and do not pretend to agree — state reality once, work with the feeling, and redirect to reality-based activity. entries.h: Which findings indicate an effective breastfeeding latch? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers The newborn's mouth covers much of the areola, not just the nipple Audible swallowing Lips flanged outward Six or more wet diapers a day after day four ↓ Reasoning A good latch is deep, quiet-lipped and audible , and the output proves it: six or more wet diapers daily once the milk is in. entries.h: Which clients should not rely on the calendar (rhythm) method alone? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers A client with irregular cycles A client who is 8 weeks postpartum A client who has just stopped depot medroxyprogesterone acetate A client approaching menopause with changing cycle lengths ↓ Reasoning Calendar counting assumes ovulation about 14 days before the next period , so it fails whenever cycles are unpredictable: irregular cycles, after childbirth, while breastfeeding, after stopping hormones, near menarche, and in perimenopause . Clinical detail A client with two years of regular cycles is the one it can work for. entries.h: Which intervention should the nurse include for a client who has heart failure?
entries.t: Answer Weigh daily and restrict fluid and sodium ↓ Reasoning Daily weight is the single most useful measure - a gain of about 1 kg (2 lb) in a day or 2.5 kg (5 lb) in a week means fluid is building before you can see it. entries.h: A client with tense ascites had a paracentesis with 5 L of fluid removed. Which finding indicates the procedure was effective and the client is stable?

entries.h: A 2-year-old's blood lead level returns at 12 mcg/dL. Which nursing action does the nurse anticipate?
entries.t: Answer Confirm with a venous level, find and remove the lead source, and recheck ↓ Reasoning Any level above 5 mcg/dL is abnormal , so 12 needs action now: confirm it with a venous sample, find and remove the lead source (old paint, dust, soil), offer iron- and calcium-rich foods, and recheck. Clinical detail Chelation is reserved for 45 mcg/dL or higher (CDC), which is why starting it now is the trap. entries.h: Which statements about tolerance and neuroadaptation in substance use disorders are accurate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Receptor downregulation means larger doses are needed for the same effect Withdrawal symptoms generally represent rebound in the direction opposite the drug's acute effect Cross-tolerance allows a benzodiazepine to treat alcohol withdrawal Repeated use shifts control from reward-driven to habit and compulsion circuitry ↓ Reasoning Tolerance reflects receptor downregulation and signaling adaptation, withdrawal is rebound in the opposite direction, cross-tolerance at the GABA receptor is why benzodiazepines substitute for alcohol, and chronic use shifts control toward dorsal striatal habit circuits. Clinical detail Tolerance is not uniform: tolerance to euphoria outpaces tolerance to respiratory depression, which is the core reason relapse after abstinence causes fatal overdose. Neuroadaptation also persists for weeks to months, sustaining craving long after detox. entries.h: Dr. K teaches, 'If you delay the priority intervention, what complication are you allowing to happen?' For a patient with a bowel obstruction, which chain of complications is the nurse allowing?
entries.t: Answer Ischemia → necrosis → perforation → sepsis ↓ Reasoning IN A BOWEL OBSTRUCTION, BLOOD FLOW IS COMPROMISED FIRST — ISCHEMIA LEADS TO DEAD TISSUE (NECROSIS), WHICH PERFORATES, WHICH SEEDS THE PERITONEUM AND ENDS IN SEPSIS. Clinical detail The fistula → abscess → sepsis chain belongs to Crohn's disease, and toxic megacolon with ulceration belongs to ulcerative colitis. The metastasis chain is colorectal cancer, which leads to obstruction and then to perforation or metastasis. Every one of these chains ends in the same place, which is exactly why the instructor says different diseases share the same complication and the same treatment. entries.h: Which situations would cause a high-pressure ventilator alarm? Select all that apply.

entries.h: A client with cirrhosis has grade 3 esophageal varices and a platelet count of 68,000 per microliter. Which complication is this client most at risk for?
entries.t: Answer Massive bleeding from the varices ↓ Reasoning Large varices are thin-walled vessels under portal pressure, and a platelet count of 68,000 removes the ability to clot, so exsanguinating hemorrhage is the dominant risk. Clinical detail The tempting option is peptic stricture, since both involve the esophagus, but stricture develops slowly from acid reflux and is not driven by portal hypertension. Obstruction and pseudocyst are not consequences of cirrhosis with varices. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client at 7 weeks gestation who reports sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain. The nurse suspects a ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Which findings support this suspicion?

entries.h: Match each client situation with the position the nurse should use.
entries.t: What the finding means Keeping the head of the bed at 30 to 45 degrees during tube feeding is the standard aspiration precaution described in the aspiration risk literature. Clinical detail Side-lying lets vomit drain out of the mouth instead of into the airway, and sitting nearly upright gives the lungs the most room to expand. Log rolling keeps a newly fused spine from twisting. Trendelenburg is the trap because it was once taught for shock; it pushes abdominal contents against the diaphragm and is not a routine nursing position. entries.h: A nurse is discharging a client hospitalized for ACUTE diverticulitis. Which dietary recommendation should the nurse emphasize to support healing during the acute inflammatory phase?
entries.t: Answer Follow a clear liquid diet and gradually advance as tolerated ↓ Reasoning ACUTE flare = bowel rest. Clinical detail Clear liquids first, then advance to LOW fiber, and only return to a HIGH-fiber diet once the diverticulitis has resolved (high fiber is for preventing new diverticula long-term, not for treating a flare). Test-taking shortcut: options 1, 3, and 4 are all essentially “high fiber” — when three answers say the same thing, they can’t all be right, so cross them off. entries.t: What the finding means ST elevation in II, III, and aVF points to an inferior wall infarction, and the reperfusion clock starts now; the usual door-to-balloon target is under 90 minutes and an ECG is obtained within 10 minutes of arrival. entries.h: The client is lying supine on the exam table for a nonstress test when she suddenly reports dizziness and nausea. BP drops from 118/72 to 88/54 mm Hg , pulse is 110/min, and her skin is pale and diaphoretic. Fetal heart rate is 150/min with moderate variability.
entries.t: What the finding means After about 20 weeks gestation, lying supine lets the gravid uterus compress the inferior vena cava and aorta, dropping venous return and blood pressure; repositioning to the left lateral side relieves the compression and is the priority action. Clinical detail Anaphylaxis and amniotic fluid embolism cause different findings (hives or sudden dyspnea and coagulopathy), and preeclampsia causes hypertension, not a sudden hypotensive drop, so these are not the best explanation here. After repositioning, the nurse rechecks blood pressure and fetal heart rate to confirm the compression has resolved for both mother and fetus; continuing the test supine or elevating the head while still supine would not relieve the compression. entries.h: Which foods should the nurse tell a client taking levodopa for Parkinson's disease to limit?

Preeclampsia is new hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or qualifying organ dysfunction, can develop postpartum, and proteinuria is not required when other diagnostic features are present. entries.h: A client is 3 hr out from a lumbar puncture. The client reports a throbbing headache that gets worse on sitting up and eases when lying flat . entries.t: What the finding means A headache that is worse upright and better flat after a lumbar puncture is caused by cerebrospinal fluid leaking from the needle site. Clinical detail Staying flat and drinking fluids lowers the pressure difference and supports fluid replacement, so that is the first action. Sitting up or walking makes the leak headache worse, and withholding fluids works against replacing what was lost. If it does not resolve, an epidural blood patch seals the leak; there is no sign of herniation here, and draining more fluid would deepen the problem. entries.h: A client who has taken alprazolam 2 mg three times daily for 4 years abruptly stopped the medication 2 days ago. Which complication is this client most at risk for?
entries.t: Answer Generalized tonic-clonic seizures ↓ Reasoning Abrupt cessation of long-term high-dose benzodiazepines removes GABA-mediated inhibition and produces a hyperexcitable central nervous system, with seizures the major life-threatening risk ; benzodiazepines must always be tapered. entries.h: A 26-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder is on day 5 of an inpatient stay. Twenty minutes after a visit ended early, she is found in the bathroom with three shallow forearm cuts made with a broken hair clip. Bleeding has stopped. She says she does not want to die, then adds that the nurse is the only one who understands and asks her not to tell the team.
entries.t: What the finding means Superficial cuts without suicidal intent still predict more self-injury, so safety and removal of means come before wound care or coping work. Clinical detail Impaired skin integrity is the tempting condition because it is the visible one, but three shallow cuts that have stopped bleeding are not what can hurt her tonight. Agreeing to keep a secret from the team is the trap; it feels caring, it splits the staff, and it removes the people who would keep her safe. entries.h: Case 9C · Thirty minutes into hemodialysis Mrs. Alvarez develops a headache, nausea, and confusion. The nurse suspects:
entries.t: Published infographic · AJKD Blog / NephMadness 2026 Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome: how rapid solute removal can affect the brain. Look for the water shift and the neurologic clues. Open the publisher’s infographic full size ↗ · Publisher and credits Original NUR 198 hemodialysis review: Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome: signs and first actions · Open full-size picture Answer Disequilibrium syndrome ↓ Reasoning During or shortly after hemodialysis, urea may fall faster in blood than in the brain. Water shifts into brain tissue. New restlessness, headache, nausea, or confusion warrants immediate assessment and notification of the dialysis team; escalate severe neurologic changes as an emergency. Clinical detail Slow the exchange rate. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Simple Nursing · Seizures and epilepsy (13:04) Why the other answers do not fit Air embolism Air entering the circulation typically raises concern for abrupt dyspnea, chest pain, or hypotension. The headache, nausea, and confusion during solute removal fit DDS more closely. Hypoglycemia Low glucose can also cause confusion. entries.h: A client with anorexia nervosa is admitted at 68 percent of ideal body weight. Which findings does the nurse expect from starvation physiology?
entries.t: Answers Bradycardia and hypotension Hypothermia with cold intolerance Lanugo hair on the trunk and face Amenorrhea from suppressed gonadotropin release Osteopenia from low estrogen and poor calcium intake ↓ Reasoning Starvation drives a hypometabolic state: the body slows the heart and drops blood pressure and temperature to conserve energy, grows lanugo for insulation, and shuts down the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis causing amenorrhea, while chronic estrogen deficiency and low calcium intake produce osteopenia . Clinical detail Hypertension with tachycardia is the opposite of this picture. Bradycardia and orthostasis are the vital signs that most often trigger medical admission. entries.h: A client arrives with right facial droop, slurred speech, and right arm drift that began about 40 minutes ago. Blood pressure is 168/94 mm Hg, blood glucose is 118 mg/dL, and the client is alert. NIHSS score is 12.
entries.t: What the finding means Because the deficits are ongoing at 40 minutes with a high NIHSS score of 12 (severe stroke), the client must be treated as an acute ischemic stroke rather than waiting to see if symptoms resolve into a TIA; a normal glucose of 118 mg/dL rules out a hypoglycemic cause, and there is no seizure history to suggest Todd's paralysis. Clinical detail A stat noncontrast CT and preparing for possible alteplase are the priority actions, since imaging must rule out hemorrhage before any thrombolytic or antiplatelet is given; giving aspirin before imaging or aggressively lowering blood pressure could worsen an undiagnosed hemorrhagic bleed or drop cerebral perfusion. Blood pressure (reporting over 185/110 mm Hg) and oxygen saturation (keeping above 94%) are the priority parameters, not potassium, uric acid, or ketones, which are unrelated to acute stroke monitoring. entries.h: A 4-year-old boy is admitted for IV antibiotics, and his peripheral IV will be started in 30 minutes. Which of the following actions should the nurse take now? (Select all that apply.)
entries.t: Answers Explain what will happen in short, concrete words just before the start Let him handle safe equipment and practice the steps on a doll Ask his caregiver to stay with him during the IV start ↓ Reasoning Preschoolers think in magical, literal terms and fear bodily harm, so preparation is simple, concrete, and given close to the event rather than hours ahead. Clinical detail Handling the equipment and rehearsing on a doll turns a frightening procedure into something he has some control over, and the caregiver's presence lowers his stress more than any distraction the nurse can offer. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client recently diagnosed with aplastic anemia. Which interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Encourage frequent hand washing and use of a mask. Prepare the client for blood transfusions as prescribed. entries.h: A nurse is assessing a client on the first postoperative day after an open cholecystectomy. Which of the following findings should the nurse identify as EXPECTED?

entries.h: A nurse is providing teaching to a client who is starting lithium carbonate. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
entries.t: Answers Drink 2 to 3 L of fluid each day Maintain a consistent daily sodium intake Avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen unless approved by the provider Notify the provider before starting a thiazide diuretic Have blood levels drawn as scheduled ↓ Reasoning Lithium is excreted by the kidneys and competes with sodium, so adequate fluid intake, consistent sodium intake, avoidance of NSAIDs and thiazide diuretics (both raise lithium levels), and scheduled level monitoring are essential. entries.h: A client has had eight negative workups for abdominal pain and remains genuinely distressed and functionally impaired. Which mechanism best explains somatic symptom disorder, and how does it differ from malingering?
entries.t: Answer Central sensitization and sensory amplification make normal signals feel intensely painful, and the distress is not consciously produced, unlike malingering's deliberate external gain ↓ Reasoning In somatic symptom disorder, central sensitization lowers the threshold of pain-processing pathways and attentional amplification magnifies benign bodily signals, so the suffering is real and not consciously generated. Clinical detail Malingering is intentional symptom production for external gain such as money or avoiding work, and factitious disorder is intentional production for the internal reward of the sick role. The nurse validates the symptom experience, avoids repeat unnecessary testing, and schedules regular brief visits rather than symptom-triggered ones. entries.h: A veteran with posttraumatic stress disorder has attended trauma-focused therapy for 3 months. Which finding indicates that the treatment has been effective?

entries.t: Answer Platelet count of 95,000/mm3 ↓ Reasoning HELLP is a laboratory diagnosis : hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and platelets under 100,000 , so 95,000 qualifies. entries.h: Highlight the findings that indicate this client may be developing myxedema coma.
entries.t: What the finding means Myxedema coma presents with a decreasing level of consciousness, low cardiac output (hypothermia, bradycardia, and hypotension), hypoventilation, and abdominal pain, all of which are present in this client. entries.h: Turning every two hours, hourly incentive spirometry while awake, and ankle pumps were started 48 hours ago. Highlight the findings that show the plan is NOT working.
entries.t: What the finding means The plan is already running, so this question asks for evidence that it is failing. The heel is the trap for anyone who checks only the sacrum, since NPIAP prevention guidance calls for floating the heels off the bed. entries.h: A client has endometritis 48 hr after a cesarean birth. Which finding should the nurse anticipate? Normal: WBC can reach 20,000 to 25,000/mm³ after birth
entries.t: Answer Heart rate 110/min ↓ Reasoning Tachycardia is the one to expect. Clinical detail Fever drives the pulse up, and it stands out all the more after a birth, because the normal postpartum pulse runs slow — puerperal bradycardia — so 110/min is a long way from where it should be. It travels with chills, fatigue, anorexia, pelvic pain, a tender uterus and foul-smelling lochia . The trap is judging the other three against non-pregnant ranges. A white count of 8,000/mm³ looks normal, but ordinary postpartum leukocytosis runs 20,000–25,000/mm³ in the first days, so 8,000 is below what this client should have — which is also why a white count is a poor infection marker in this first week. The ESR is normally raised in pregnancy and the puerperium, so 15 mm/hr is unremarkable too. Respirations of 18/min are simply normal. entries.h: the course teaches, 'If you delay the priority intervention, what complication are you allowing to happen?' For a patient with a bowel obstruction, which chain of complications is the nurse allowing?
entries.t: Answer Ischemia → necrosis → perforation → sepsis ↓ Reasoning IN A BOWEL OBSTRUCTION, BLOOD FLOW IS COMPROMISED FIRST — ISCHEMIA LEADS TO DEAD TISSUE (NECROSIS), WHICH PERFORATES, WHICH SEEDS THE PERITONEUM AND ENDS IN SEPSIS. entries.h: Which assessment findings best support the nurse's conclusion that Mrs. Garcia has a fecal impaction with constipation?
entries.t: Answers No bowel movement for 6 days Hypoactive bowel sounds A small amount of liquid stool in her brief ↓ Reasoning Three findings tie this together: six days without a stool means stool has sat in the colon long enough for more water to be absorbed and harden it, hypoactive sounds mean slow intestinal motility, and the liquid stool is OVERFLOW DIARRHEA LEAKING AROUND THE HARD IMPACTED STOOL. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client receiving total parenteral nutrition (TPN) through a central line. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Verify the TPN bag label and prescription with a second nurse Monitor daily weights and intake/output Monitor blood glucose levels every 4 hours Have 10–20% dextrose available if the next TPN bag is delayed ↓ Reasoning Independent double-check applies to high-alert therapies — yes. Clinical detail Daily weights and I&O track fluid and nutritional response — yes. Glucose q4h — yes, because TPN delivers a heavy carbohydrate load and causes HYPERglycemia. Keeping dextrose available — yes: if TPN stops abruptly the client’s already-elevated insulin keeps working and they crash into HYPOglycemia. The wrong ones: TPN needs a DEDICATED lumen (a central line has several — just don’t share the TPN one). Tubing and bag change is every 24 HOURS, not 48 — this is essentially IV food and it grows bacteria. A filter is ALWAYS used, not just with lipids. Flushing before and after “use” only applies to intermittent (usually home) TPN — standard hospital TPN runs continuously, so there is no before or after. Advice from lecture on that last one: if you’ve never heard of it, leave it unselected. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Why the other answers do not fit Administer medications through the TPN line to reduce line access The wrong ones: TPN needs a DEDICATED lumen (a central line has several — just don’t share the TPN one). Use IV tubing with a filter only if lipids are included A filter is ALWAYS used, not just with lipids. Flush the TPN line with saline before and after use The wrong ones: TPN needs a DEDICATED lumen (a central line has several — just don’t share the TPN one). entries.h: A client currently has normal hemoglobin levels, but significantly decreased SaO2 and PaO2 levels. What is an implication of this physiologic state?
entries.t: Answer The client's tissue demands may be met, but the client will be unable to respond to physiological stressors. ↓ Reasoning With a normal hemoglobin level of 15 mg/dL and a PaO2 level of 40 mm Hg (SaO2 75%), there is adequate oxygen available for the tissues, but no reserve for physiologic stresses that increase tissue oxygen demand. Clinical detail If a serious incident occurs (e.g., bronchospasm, aspiration, hypotension, or cardiac dysrhythmias) that reduces the intake of oxygen from the lungs, tissue hypoxia results. entries.h: A nurse is leading a community education session on colorectal cancer prevention. Which risk factors should the nurse identify as significant? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Regular use of tobacco products Diet high in red meat Family history of colorectal cancer Frequent drinking of alcohol ↓ Reasoning Smokers swallow carcinogens, raising both gastric and colorectal cancer risk. Family history matters enough that some inherited syndromes lead people to elect a prophylactic colectomy — those families can develop colon cancer in their 30s. entries.h: A nurse is teaching a client about the potential complications of frequent laxative use. Which should the nurse include?

entries.h: Respiratory rate is 68/min with grunting, nasal flaring, and intercostal retractions, plus mild cyanosis. Axillary temperature is 36.9°C, and blood glucose is 58 mg/dL. Normal: newborn blood glucose above 40 to 45 mg/dL
entries.t: What the finding means A preterm newborn at 32 weeks with a respiratory rate over 60/min, grunting, nasal flaring, and retractions has the classic presentation of RDS from insufficient surfactant, not sepsis (which would show temperature instability and poor feeding), cold stress (temperature is within the expected range here), or a tracheesophageal fistula (which causes choking and excess secretions with feeding rather than this picture). Clinical detail Obtaining an ABG and chest x-ray confirms the diagnosis and severity, and surfactant replacement is the definitive treatment, while oral feeding is unsafe with this degree of distress and withholding respiratory support would allow deterioration. Oxygen saturation and respiratory rate/effort are the two parameters that most directly track whether the newborn is responding to treatment. entries.h: Why do respiratory infections cause more obstruction in children than in adults?

entries.h: A mother reports her newborn had bloody mucus in the stool earlier and is worried. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Assess the colour, amount and consistency of the stool Teach her how the stools will change over the next few days, and to report it if the blood continues Document it and notify the provider immediately ↓ Reasoning Look first, then report. Clinical detail Blood in a newborn’s stool is reported promptly — the day you see it, not after waiting to see if it clears. It is often swallowed maternal blood from the birth or a cracked nipple, but only the provider’s workup can say so. So see the stool first — colour, amount and consistency — note how she looks and feeds, then document and notify . Then give her the map: meconium (thick, tarry, dark green-black) for the first day or two, transitional (greenish-brown, looser) around days 3 to 4, then milk stools — seedy and mustard-yellow if breastfed, paler and firmer if formula-fed — and ask her to report any further blood straight away. “That's normal” or “it should settle by day 3” is a reassurance nobody can give before the workup , and it dismisses her. Nothing here warrants NPO. entries.h: Which rights does a client hospitalized on a psychiatric unit retain? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers The right to be treated with dignity and respect The right to give or refuse informed consent for treatment The right to confidentiality of health information The right to the least restrictive treatment environment ↓ Reasoning Psychiatric clients do not lose their rights simply because they have a mental illness: dignity, informed consent, confidentiality, and the least restrictive setting all continue. entries.h: A paranoid client refuses all meals, stating that the kitchen staff are poisoning the food. Which nursing intervention is best?
entries.t: Answer Offer sealed, unopened food and canned beverages and let the client open them ↓ Reasoning Sealed, unopened items the client opens themselves give control and bypass the delusion without arguing about it — this is the most-tested paranoia intervention. Clinical detail Explaining is arguing. A different entrée doesn’t address the fear. Tasting the client’s food is a boundary violation and can also be interpreted as proof the nurse knows which portion is safe. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Why the other answers do not fit Explain that all trays come from the same kitchen and no one is being poisoned Arguing over whether the food is poisoned can increase mistrust and does not help the client eat. Document refusal and notify dietary to send a different entrée Changing the entrée leaves the fear of tampering unresolved. Sit with the client and taste a bite of the food to demonstrate it is safe Tasting the food can reinforce the idea that it must be tested. Opening a sealed item gives the client control without endorsing the belief. Original Study Hub illustration · Schizophrenia: symptoms and therapeutic response. Open full size

entries.h: A client started haloperidol 3 days ago and now cannot sit still, paces continuously, and says he feels an unbearable inner restlessness. What is the most likely cause of these findings?

Clinical detail Worsening psychosis is the most dangerous distractor because misreading akathisia as agitation leads to increasing the very drug causing it, which worsens the symptom and is associated with suicide risk. entries.h: A client at 32 weeks of gestation reports heartburn, calf cramps, constipation, and backache. Which suggestions by the nurse are appropriate? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers "Eat small, frequent meals and stay upright after eating." "When a leg cramp starts, dorsiflex your foot." "Increase fiber and fluids and keep walking each day." ↓ Reasoning Progesterone relaxes the esophageal sphincter, so small meals and staying upright help heartburn; leg cramps are relieved by dorsiflexing the foot ; and slowed motility plus iron is managed with fiber, fluids, and walking. Clinical detail Pointing the toes feels like the natural stretch but worsens the cramp , and backache is treated with pelvic tilt, low heels, and side-lying — not supine positioning. Shared reasoning for choices without a separate note: Progesterone relaxes the esophageal sphincter, so small meals and staying upright help heartburn; leg cramps are relieved by dorsiflexing the foot ; and slowed motility plus iron is managed with fiber, fluids, and walking. A female pelvic anatomy diagram labels normal endometrium inside the uterine cavity and endometriosis lesions on the outer uterine surface, an ovary, the pelvic lining and the fallopian tube, with an ovarian endometrioma labelled as a chocolate cyst and an adhesion. Symptoms listed: painful periods, chronic pelvic pain, deep pain with sex, bowel and bladder pain especially during periods, fatigue and possible fertility difficulty, and that some people have very few symptoms. Assessment: pain and menstrual history, pelvic examination and imaging such as ultrasound or MRI, normal imaging does not exclude endometriosis, and a clinical diagnosis can guide treatment while laparoscopy may be appropriate in selected cases. Treatment depends on symptoms and fertility goals: pain relief, hormonal suppression, surgery, with supportive symptom tracking and pelvic floor or pain care. Key distinctions: endometriosis occurs outside the uterus, adenomyosis occurs within the uterine muscle, pregnancy and hysterectomy are not guaranteed cures, and pain severity does not reliably match lesion extent. entries.h: Twenty-four hours after sustaining a femoral shaft fracture, a young adult becomes dyspneic and confused and has petechiae across the chest and axillae. What is the most likely cause of these findings?
entries.t: Answer Fat embolism syndrome ↓ Reasoning The triad of hypoxia, neurologic change, and a petechial rash appearing 12 to 72 hours after a long bone fracture is diagnostic of fat embolism syndrome. entries.h: A nurse is caring for a client with a subclavian central line. Which actions reduce the client's risk of a central line-associated bloodstream infection? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Scrub the hub with friction for 15 seconds before every access Change the transparent dressing every 7 days, or sooner if it is damp, loose or soiled Review the line every day and remove it as soon as it is no longer needed ↓ Reasoning Scrub the hub 15 seconds with friction, change the transparent dressing every 7 days (gauze every 2 days, either one sooner if damp, loose or soiled), and pull the line the day it stops being needed — that last one prevents more infections than any technique. Clinical detail Why 2 minutes is wrong here: the chlorhexidine–alcohol prep has two times, and the site decides which one. Dry site (chest, arm, abdomen — so a subclavian line) = 30 seconds of back-and-forth friction. Moist site (groin, axilla — a femoral line) = 2 minutes . Either way, let it dry completely ; the drying is what kills, not the wiping. This client has a subclavian line, so 30 seconds. Drawing blood from the line does not itself cause CLABSI — poor technique at the hub does. And femoral is the highest -infection site, not a request you would make. Original Study Hub review graphic · based on the quiz explanation Why the other answers do not fit Scrub the chlorhexidine prep for a full 2 minutes at each dressing change Why 2 minutes is wrong here: the chlorhexidine–alcohol prep has two times, and the site decides which one. entries.h: A laboring client has the following fetal strip. Which intervention by the nurse is appropriate?

entries.h: Four clients were involved in the same apartment building fire. Which client is at greatest risk for developing posttraumatic stress disorder?
entries.t: Answer A woman with a history of childhood sexual abuse and prior depression who was trapped in her unit, believed she would die, and lives alone ↓ Reasoning The strongest predictors of PTSD are prior trauma, preexisting psychiatric illness, perceived life threat during the event, and lack of social support , and this client has all four. entries.h: A nurse is calculating intake and output for a client with continuous bladder irrigation. Which is correct?
entries.t: Correct answer Subtract the irrigant volume so it is not counted in intake or output Why The irrigant is not counted in I&O - it goes in and comes right back out, so including it invents both intake and urine that never existed. Subtract the irrigation volume from total drainage to get true urine output. Why the other answers do not fit Count the irrigant as intake and all drainage as output Irrigant enters through the catheter and returns to the bag. Counting it as patient intake and urine makes both totals falsely high. Count only half the irrigant as intake There is no half-volume adjustment. Record the measured irrigation separately and subtract the full infused volume from total drainage. Count the irrigant as output only The bag contains irrigant plus urine. Treating irrigant as urine output overstates kidney output. Original Study Hub memory visual · Flowing pink drainage, bright blood with clots, and stopped outflow. entries.h: One hour after birth the nurse finds the fundus boggy and displaced to the right of the umbilicus. What should the nurse do first?
entries.t: Answer Have the client empty her bladder ↓ Reasoning A fundus that is displaced to one side is being pushed there by a full bladder , which also prevents the uterus from contracting down. entries.h: The parent of a 5-month-old with good head and neck control asks when to start baby foods. Which points should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Introduce one new food each week Continue breast milk or iron-fortified formula Watch for signs of food allergy or GI intolerance ↓ Reasoning Solids start at 4 to 6 months, once head and neck control is there — which this baby has. Clinical detail One new food at a time is the whole method: if a rash, vomiting or diarrhea follows, the parent knows exactly which food to blame, and one food at a time is gentler on an immature gut. Cow's milk does not belong before 12 months — it lacks the iron and the nutrient balance an infant needs and can irritate the gut. Introducing three foods at once defeats the point of introducing them singly, and waiting until 12 months to start solids is far too late. entries.h: A client with bulimia nervosa who vomits several times daily has a potassium of 2.8 mEq/L. Which acid-base and cardiac consequence should the nurse anticipate?

entries.h: An older adult with type 2 diabetes and several days of poor oral intake is admitted confused and profoundly dehydrated. Test Result Normal range Blood glucose 648 mg/dL 70–110 mg/dL (fasting) Arterial pH 7.36 7.35–7.45 Bicarbonate 19 mEq/L 22–26 mEq/L Serum osmolarity 328 mOsm/L 275–295 mOsm/L Blood and urine ketones Negative Negative
entries.t: What the finding means A glucose over 600 mg/dL, an osmolarity above 320 mOsm/L, no significant acidosis (pH over 7.3, bicarbonate over 15 mEq/L), and negative ketones together define HHS rather than DKA, which would show ketosis and a pH under 7.3. Clinical detail Somogyi effect and dawn phenomenon are patterns of overnight glucose swings, not an acute crisis like this. Large-volume isotonic fluids and an IV insulin infusion are the priority treatments; bicarbonate is reserved for severe acidosis that is not present here, and switching to subcutaneous insulin or restricting fluids would leave this profoundly dehydrated client under-treated. Potassium shifts rapidly once fluids and insulin start, and neurologic status reflects the client's dangerously high osmolarity, making these the priority parameters over ketones, ABG pH, or uric acid. entries.h: What are the critical points when assessing the respiratory rate of a 1-year-old? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Obtain the respiratory rate first Let the child stay in the parent's arms or a position of comfort An average rate for this age is about 30 breaths per minute ↓ Reasoning Least invasive first. Clinical detail Counting breaths needs nothing but your eyes, so it goes before the stethoscope, the cuff and the thermometer — every one of those means touching the child, and a crying toddler's respiratory rate is not his respiratory rate. For the same reason he stays in the parent's arms . A 1-year-old runs about 20 to 40 , averaging around 30 . Watch the abdomen, not the chest. Children under about 6 are diaphragmatic breathers — the belly is what moves, and counting chest rise loses breaths. And count a full minute, never 30 seconds doubled : infant and toddler breathing is normally irregular, so a half-minute count doubles the error along with the number. Undressing him fully is neither necessary nor kind in a cool room — and cold is its own problem. entries.h: A nurse on the antepartum unit is caring for four clients who have preeclampsia. Which finding indicates that the client requires further assessment and intervention? Normal: urine protein under 300 mg in 24 hours
entries.t: Answer Deep tendon reflexes 4+ ↓ Reasoning Deep tendon reflexes of 4+ (hyperreflexia, often with clonus) mean the central nervous system is irritable and a seizure (eclampsia) may be coming, so this client needs assessment and intervention now. Clinical detail Proteinuria under 0.3 g in 24 hours is below the preeclampsia threshold, and 144/90 is the expected mild-range pressure of preeclampsia. Your ATI book counts oliguria as a severe feature at less than 500 mL in 24 hours , so 650 mL does not meet it. Do not confuse that with the less than 30 mL/hr stop rule for a client on magnesium sulfate : 650 mL/24 hr is about 27 mL/hr, which is why that option tempts, but this question gives no magnesium and the reflexes are the clear danger sign. Original Study Hub illustration · Preeclampsia versus eclampsia, the same spectrum with different presentations. Preeclampsia is new hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or qualifying organ dysfunction, can develop postpartum, and proteinuria is not required when other diagnostic features are present. Eclampsia is new seizures associated with preeclampsia when another cause does not explain them, and can occur without previously recognised preeclampsia. entries.h: A client who has HIV and reports consistent antiretroviral adherence returns for follow-up labs. Test Result Normal range CD4 count 180 cells/mm3 (down from prior visit) 500–1,200 cells/mm3 CD4:CD8 ratio 0.6 2:1 HIV viral load Rising over the past 3 months None detected (goal of treatment)
entries.t: What the finding means A CD4:CD8 ratio under 1 signals severe disease, and a falling CD4 count with a rising viral load despite reported adherence suggests the current regimen is failing, most likely from drug resistance. Clinical detail The provider needs to be notified so resistance testing can guide a regimen change; the client should never simply stop antiretroviral therapy, since that removes viral suppression entirely and worsens outcomes. Dismissing the trend as normal fluctuation is incorrect because a ratio of 0.6 with a rising viral load on therapy is a concerning, not benign, pattern. entries.h: The nurse is teaching a client with allergic rhinitis about the safe and effective use of medications. Which information would be the most essential to give this client about preventing possible drug interactions?
entries.t: Answer Read drug labels carefully before taking OTC medications. ↓ Reasoning Client education is essential when assisting the client in the use of all medications. Clinical detail To prevent possible drug interactions, the client is cautioned to read drug labels before taking any OTC medications. Some websites are reliable and valid information sources, but this is not always the case. The face and neck are flushed and sweaty, the nose is congested, and the skin below the injury is cool with goose bumps. Heart rate is 48/min. The indwelling catheter bag has 30 mL of urine from the last 6 hr.
entries.t: What the finding means A pounding headache with severe hypertension, flushing and sweating above the lesion, and a slow heart rate in a client injured above T6 is autonomic dysreflexia, and the nearly empty drainage bag points to a blocked catheter as the trigger. Clinical detail Sitting the client up drops the pressure by gravity, and clearing the obstruction removes the stimulus driving the episode. Lying flat or adding a binder and stockings raises pressure further, which treats neurogenic or spinal shock, not this; the bradycardia is a reflex to the high pressure and stops when the trigger is gone, so atropine is not the fix. Blood pressure and bladder volume are the two numbers that show whether the emergency is resolving. entries.h: Which statement about burn depth and pain is accurate?
entries.t: Answer A deep full-thickness burn may hurt less in the center because the nerve endings are destroyed ↓ Reasoning “The worst burn should hurt the most” is false , and it is a favourite exam trap. entries.h: A client presents to the ED with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and abdominal distension. The client has a history of MULTIPLE abdominal surgeries. Which is the priority nursing intervention?
entries.t: Answer Insert a nasogastric tube ↓ Reasoning Pull the cues from the stem: pain + vomiting + DISTENSION = bowel obstruction, and a history of multiple abdominal surgeries means ADHESIONS, which are the classic cause of recurrent obstruction. Clinical detail An NG tube DECOMPRESSES the GI tract by suctioning out air and fluid — uncomfortable to place, but it relieves the distension and vomiting. Oral fluids are pointless when the client is vomiting behind an obstruction. Ambulation increases peristalsis against a blockage and isn’t realistic in severe pain. Paracentesis drains ASCITES — that’s a cirrhosis intervention, and this client has distension from gas and fluid trapped in bowel, not free peritoneal fluid. Oral fluids are pointless when the client is vomiting behind an obstruction. Ambulation increases peristalsis against a blockage and isn’t realistic in severe pain. entries.h: A client has been on bed rest for 3 weeks. Which musculoskeletal changes should the nurse anticipate?
entries.t: Answer Muscle atrophy, joint contractures, and bone loss ↓ Reasoning Unused muscle wastes away, joints stiffen into contractures, and bone demineralizes without weight-bearing stress. Clinical detail Rest does not build muscle or bone - it is the loading that maintains them, which is why ROM and early mobility are nursing priorities. entries.h: A 52-year-old is starting morphine PCA after abdominal surgery. Which statements should the nurse include in teaching?
entries.t: Answers You are the only person who should ever press the PCA button. We will start a stimulant laxative such as senna to prevent constipation. We will check your sedation level and respiratory rate on a regular schedule. ↓ Reasoning PCA IS CLIENT-CONTROLLED ONLY; FAMILY MUST NEVER PUSH THE BUTTON, because the built-in safety is that an oversedated client cannot dose himself. Clinical detail Opioid constipation needs a STIMULANT laxative like senna or bisacodyl, not fiber alone. Needing more drug over time is TOLERANCE and withdrawal on stopping is physical DEPENDENCE; addiction is compulsive use despite harm. Sedation and respiratory rate are monitored every time. entries.h: A nurse is reviewing four clients receiving antipsychotics. Which client is at greatest risk for tardive dyskinesia?

entries.h: Which points should the nurse include in teaching? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers Give oral rehydration solution in small amounts frequently, even if he vomits Count wet diapers and report fewer than expected for his age Continue breast or formula feeding through the illness Return immediately if he becomes floppy, sleepy or hard to wake ↓ Reasoning Small frequent volumes are absorbed even when a child vomits, which is why 5 mL every few minutes by syringe works. entries.h: A client taking a loop diuretic has a serum potassium of 3 mEq/L. Which assessment finding fits that result?
entries.t: Answer A quiet, distended abdomen with hypoactive bowel sounds ↓ Reasoning Potassium runs every muscle, including the smooth muscle of the gut - so when it falls the bowel slows to a stop : hypoactive sounds, distension, constipation, sometimes a full ileus. Clinical detail Carpopedal spasm is low calcium , and peaked T waves are high potassium. The 6 Ls are worth holding on to: lethargy, leg cramps, limp muscles, low shallow respirations, lethal dysrhythmias, lots of urine. entries.h: A client whose vaginal and rectal culture at 36 weeks was positive for group B streptococcus was admitted at 2200 with ruptured membranes. Her first IV dose of penicillin G was hung at 0500, and she gave birth at 0645.

entries.h: A nurse is teaching students about the three fetal shunts. Which statements should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers The ductus venosus bypasses the liver. The foramen ovale sends blood from the right atrium directly to the left atrium. The ductus arteriosus connects the pulmonary artery to the aorta. The shunts exist because the fetal lungs are full of fluid and do no work in utero. ↓ Reasoning All three shunts are shortcuts around the fluid-filled, nonworking fetal lungs : ductus venosus past the liver, foramen ovale right atrium to left atrium, and ductus arteriosus pulmonary artery to aorta. Clinical detail The tempting distractor is timing; the shunts stay open through gestation and begin closing with the first breaths (the ductus arteriosus over the next few days), not in the second trimester. entries.t: Answer A client who was recently started on hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension and has been doing yard work in hot weather ↓ Reasoning Thiazide diuretics increase renal reabsorption of lithium, and heat-related fluid and sodium loss compounds it, so this client faces a double mechanism for rising lithium levels . entries.h: Match each presentation to the oncologic emergency it best represents.
entries.t: What the finding means Superior vena cava syndrome from a mediastinal tumor causes facial and periorbital edema, dyspnea, and epistaxis, and is managed by sitting the client upright and giving urgent radiation. Clinical detail Tumor lysis syndrome follows rapid cell death after chemotherapy and causes hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, and hyperuricemia, treated with large-volume fluids and allopurinol. Spinal cord compression causes worsening back pain, leg weakness, and new bowel or bladder dysfunction, requiring urgent imaging and steroids. Hypercalcemia of malignancy causes anorexia, a shortened QT interval, and kidney stones, treated with saline and a loop diuretic. Neutropenic sepsis is not used because none of these vignettes describe fever with a low neutrophil count. entries.h: A client with COPD was placed on 6 L per minute by simple mask for dyspnea. Two hours later the client is drowsy and difficult to arouse, respirations are 8 and shallow, and the oxygen saturation is 96 percent. What is the most likely cause of the change?

entries.h: The client reports severe nausea and vomiting and dark, prune-juice-colored discharge. Fundal height measures larger than expected for dates. Ultrasound shows a dense cluster of vesicles with no fetus or fetal heartbeat.
entries.t: What the finding means Hyperemesis, a uterus large for dates, prune-juice-colored bleeding, and an ultrasound showing a vesicular mass with no viable fetus are classic for gestational trophoblastic disease, not placenta previa or ectopic pregnancy, neither of which shows a vesicular mass. Clinical detail Because hCG must be trended weekly and then monthly for up to a year to rule out choriocarcinoma, and pregnancy would also raise hCG and confound that follow-up, reliable contraception is required during that period; there is no fixed 5-year pregnancy ban, and a future pregnancy is not destined to be molar again. entries.h: A 25-year-old man with a 3-year history of HIV is admitted to the medical-surgical unit with respiratory distress. 1100. A 25-year-old man who has been HIV positive for 3 years is admitted with a dry cough and a fever of 38.3°C (101.0°F). He has fatigue and shortness of breath, a respiratory rate of 28/min and an SpO₂ of 90% on room air . Breathing is slightly labored and his chest feels tight on a deep breath. He has taken antiretroviral medication since diagnosis but stopped it recently when he was laid off from his job . Three days of over-the-counter medication did not help. IV 0.9% sodium chloride is infusing in the right arm at 75 mL/hr. Labs drawn. Bronchoalveolar lavage completed, cytology pending.
entries.t: What the finding means This case walks the whole clinical judgment model in order — recognize the cues, analyze them, prioritize, generate solutions, take action, evaluate — and every step turns on the same fact: he stopped his antiretroviral medication when he lost his job. Clinical detail That is the risk factor, the reason the CD4 count has collapsed, the reason a social work referral is part of the medical plan, and the first thing to teach. Treating the pneumonia without addressing why he stopped simply schedules the next admission. entries.h: A client has a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis. The nurse is aware that neuromuscular disorders such as multiple sclerosis may lead to a decreased vital capacity. What does vital capacity measure?
entries.t: Answer The maximal volume of air exhaled from the point of maximal inspiration ↓ Reasoning Vital capacity is measured by having the client take in a maximal breath and exhale fully through a spirometer. Clinical detail Vital lung capacity is the maximal volume of air exhaled from the point of maximal inspiration, and neuromuscular disorders such as multiple sclerosis may lead to a decreased vital capacity. Tidal volume is defined as the volume of air inhaled and exhaled with each breath. The volume of air in the lungs after a maximal inspiration is the total lung capacity. Inspiratory capacity is the maximal volume of air inhaled after normal expiration. entries.h: Which findings should the nurse expect in a client who has bacterial meningitis?
entries.t: Answer A positive Brudzinski and Kernig sign with a stiff neck, fever and confusion ↓ Reasoning Brudzinski - flexing the neck makes the hips and knees flex. Clinical detail Kernig - the leg cannot be straightened once the hip is flexed. With fever, headache, photophobia and confusion. entries.h: A client is learning fertility awareness methods to plan a pregnancy. Which statements by the client indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
entries.t: Answers My temperature should rise about 0.4 to 0.8 degrees F after I ovulate. Around ovulation my cervical mucus becomes thin, clear, and stretchy. entries.h: Which client should the nurse recognize as having the greatest risk for developing a pulmonary embolism?

entries.h: Highlight the findings that suggest this client is in pain.
entries.t: What the finding means When a client cannot self-report, observed behavior is the assessment.
